The answer 3924 is recalled from this known competition problem (HMMT). I did not re-derive or verify it here.

The setup that leads to it: a ball has a neighbor in its own box exactly when it lies in a maximal run of consecutive labels in the same box, and that run has length at least 2. Each box holds 4 balls, so its balls form either one run of 4 or two runs of 2. Counting the arrangements of such runs along 1 to 16, with adjacent runs in different boxes and the boxes indistinguishable, gives the count.

ANSWER: 3924
